newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer after rangebound session.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer after rangebound session.

text.p: COMEX copper ended slightly firmer after trading within a narrow range as a bullish large drop in LME stocks was countered by the bearish return to work at the Kennecott smelter in Utah.
LME stocks fell a larger-than-expected 19,125 tonnes Friday to 172,425 tonnes, below a month's global supply.

The London exchange's copper stocks have fallen sharply in recent weeks but several analysts have said that much of the drawdown is going into off-exchange warehouses in China and not for consumption.

"There are rising expectations the metal is being consumed in China," said Bette Raptopoulos of Prudential Securities. "But because of uncertainties, the market continues to move gingerly to the upside."
Workers are Kennecott's operations in Magna, Utah were due to return to work at 1500 local time Friday after they went walked out on Wednesday.
The smelter was being operated at a reduced level by management during the brief strike. Negotiations for a new labor contract continue.
December COMEX settled 0.65 cent firmer at 91.55 cents, traded 91.70 to 90.70 cents.
Spot October ended at 94.10 cents, up 1.10 cents.
Volume was estimated at 9,000 lots compared to Thursday's official 13,169 lots.
